cuadrada.escena:
Create ONE independent, exquisite handcrafted PHYSICAL PAPER-CUT narrative artwork. The reference files are our own AI visual-bible model sheets and environments, not photographs. They supply identity and the established material language; do not reproduce their sheet layouts, alternate views or detail insets. Very expressive cut-paper construction: thick matte dyed cardstock with visible pale cut cross-sections, lifted and curled edges, actual overlaps, separated foliage strata, folded leaf midribs, folded plumage, deliberate irregular hand-cut curves, long tiny cast shadows under paper pieces, deeper shadows between environmental planes, tactile grain. Build bodies and water from quietly shaped paper surfaces; faces with a few calm cut planes, never crystalline low-poly facets. No smooth plastic, photoreal flesh, CGI toy, digital painting or generic polygon rendering. Full bleed world continuing outside all four frame edges, without visible diorama perimeter, plinth, frame or display table. No lettering, caption, watermark, border or collage. Rich restrained jungle olive, emerald, cobalt, burnt ochre and warm cream; use real differences in light and composition among the three illustrations. All principal human and animal silhouettes must be fully inside the frame, including feet, snout, tail and feather tips.

FORMAT: square 1:1, 1024 x 1024. Function HUELLA: a symbolic editorial image, not a third literal scene. Reference 1 O04 low storytelling bench shape and brown paper construction; reference 2 L03 forest/river materials only.

THESIS: reciprocity with the animal opens a passage; in this adapted tale, Jirayauma offers his father's storytelling bench in return for the Caiman's river crossing. CARRIER: ONE empty low carved storytelling bench like the LEFT full bench in O04, long gently concave single thick seat and two broad solid end supports with small arched foot notches. Entire bench and both supports visible. Do not copy all three model-sheet benches; do not invent a throne or modern upholstered chair.

ONE IMPOSSIBLE OPERATION: the brown concave seat itself opens into a continuous deep COBALT PAPER RIVER. Its left and right outer brown edges still clearly define the bench seat, but the interior of the seat has become an open river channel. That same blue channel spills over the FRONT CENTER of the seat as a generous folded paper stream, passes THROUGH the open space between the two whole solid supports, then continues across the foreground earth toward the viewer. It is ONE uninterrupted winding river made of layered thick blue paper sheets, not a painted blue cushion, cloth, closed lid, liquid fountain or disconnected puddle. Keep the full brown supports untouched and dry, the open gap between them plainly visible, and the stream continuous from seat to foreground. The impossible transformation of a seat into a river passage must read at small size.

The bench is the dominant single symbol, at about half the frame width, three-quarter frontal view in an intimate deep-emerald forest clearing. River ribbons flowing out of it are the only magical action. No person, Caiman, jaguar, feathers floating around, smoke, deity, glowing glyph, decorative medallion, extra prop or extra bench. Fine red-orange fallen leaves can quietly accent the forest, without competing symbols. Deep green paper strata surround the warm brown bench and electric blue river; soft dappled morning light differs from the other two pieces. This is an explicitly ORIGINAL EDITORIAL metaphor, not a claimed traditional Huitoto motif or literal illustration of an undocumented ritual. Full bleed forest at all edges, no white studio background.
